one_liner: CUTLASS CUDA forward kernel for Kimi Delta Attention; 1.7-3.3x lower latency than flash-linear-attention's Triton chunk_kda on H20/GB200.
what_it_does: Computes the inference forward pass of Kimi Delta Attention (KDA), a gated delta-rule linear attention with a per-channel gate, for bf16 inputs with K=V=128, fixed-length or varlen (cu_seqlens) batches, and optional bf16/fp32 recurrent state in and out. Most users never call it directly: with flash-linear-attention >= 0.5.0 installed, fla.ops.kda.chunk_kda dispatches to it automatically under torch.inference_mode() (FLA_FLASH_KDA=0 opts out). The raw API is flash_kda.fwd(q, k, v, g, beta, scale, out, A_log, dt_bias, lower_bound, ...), which writes into a preallocated out tensor.
how_it_is_fast: It uses chunk size 16 instead of FLA's 64. With the gate lower_bound at -5 this keeps exp(cumsum(g)) within bf16 range without intra-chunk rescaling, and the 16x16 inverse becomes cheap: fp32 forward substitution on two 8x8 diagonal blocks, merged with bf16 HMMA GEMMs. The work is split into a token-parallel kernel (gate activation, L2 norm, decay, L/Mqk build, inversion) and a head-parallel kernel (chunked delta-rule recurrence, output, state), which the authors say is at least 15% faster than one fused kernel. Other tricks: the on-chip state is held in bf16 but updated with fp32 FMAs; base-2 ex2.approx and tanh.approx-based sigmoid; __launch_bounds__(256,8) with shared-memory unions for occupancy; register-file transposes (MOVM) instead of shared-memory round trips; and TMA loads.
when_to_use: Serving or prefill for KDA-based models (Kimi Linear style) on Hopper or Blackwell, where fla's chunk_kda is on the critical path: about 1.85-2.3x on H20 and 1.7-3.3x on GB200 at T=8192, H=64/96.
Varlen batches of mixed sequence lengths, where the gain over the Triton kernel is largest (2.3x on H20 and 3.2-3.3x on GB200 for 8x1024 packed sequences).
Stacks already built on flash-linear-attention: install FlashKDA and chunk_kda picks it up with no code changes, as long as the call runs under torch.inference_mode().
Inference where a bf16 recurrent state is acceptable (it halves the state's memory); fp32 state in and out is also supported and is what the published tables measure.
when_not_to_use: Training: there is no backward pass, and FLA only dispatches to FlashKDA in inference mode.
Head dims other than K=V=128 (enforced by TORCH_CHECK; issue #4 asks about other sizes), non-bf16 activations, or pre-Hopper GPUs (setup.py builds only sm_90a, 100a, 103a and 120a).
Scalar-gate gated delta rule (GDN) models: that is a different algorithm, and against fla's GDN kernel FlashKDA is only 0.96x (slower, GB200 H=64 fixed) to 1.80x.

Anywhere you need a stable, released dependency: version 0.0.1, 10 commits, no PyPI wheel documented, 14 of 16 issues open, and an exact-match correctness test failing on B200 with CUDA 13.0 (#12, open).

integration.dependencies: PyTorch 2.4+ (C++/CUDA extension built with torch.utils.cpp_extension), CUTLASS (git submodule); flash-linear-attention >= 0.5.0 for auto-dispatch and for the tests and benchmarks
integration.min_toolchain: CUDA 12.9+, PyTorch 2.4+, nvcc targeting sm_90a or newer
integration.platforms: NVIDIA sm_90a (H100/H20/H200), sm_100a/sm_103a (B200/GB200/B300), sm_120a (RTX 50 / RTX PRO Blackwell); benchmarked only on H20 and GB200
integration.thread_safety: not documented; launches on PyTorch's current CUDA stream and allocates a fresh workspace (torch.empty) on each call
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — transparent replacement for fla's chunk_kda forward under torch.inference_mode() with fla >= 0.5.0; the direct API is a lower-level function with a preallocated output, bf16 only, K=V=128, forward only

gotchas: The published H20 (2026-04-22) and GB200 (2026-05-26) tables predate the fix for missing TMA proxy and mbarrier-init fences (#24/#25, 2026-07-29), which issue #24 says could cause hangs, stale data or silent corruption. They also predate the 2026-09-01 switch from an fp16 Neumann inverse to fp32 forward substitution. No re-run has been published, and issue #34 asking about the performance effect is unanswered.

lower_bound is documented as -5 to 0, but csrc/flash_kda.cpp does not check it. The chunk-16 bf16-range argument in the design doc assumes -5, so do not pass values below that without testing accuracy yourself.
In varlen mode B must be 1 and cu_seqlens int64; initial_state and final_state must share a dtype.
The default build compiles only for the GPU visible at install time and fails if none is visible; set FLASH_KDA_CUDA_ARCHS=all (or e.g. 90a,100a) for wheel or CI builds.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick FlashKDA when the model uses KDA's per-channel gate and you only need inference. FlashQLA targets the scalar-gate gated delta rule (Qwen-style GDN) and also covers backward, so it is the better fit for GDN models or training. FlashInfer's GDN prefill kernel is the option if you are already inside FlashInfer.
verified_claims_summary: BENCHMARK_H20.md and BENCHMARK_GB200.md (first-party, generated by benchmarks/generate_benchmark_md.py using CUDA-event timing, warmup 30, 200 iters x 5 repeats) report KDA forward latency at T=8192, D=128, H=96 and 64. With FlashKDA run in fp32-state mode against fla's Triton chunk_kda, the speedup is 1.85-2.31x on H20 and 1.70-3.27x on GB200, largest for varlen batches. No fla, PyTorch or CUDA versions, driver or host CPU are recorded, and the numbers predate later correctness fixes.
status_note: Active but early (v0.0.1, last commit 2026-09-01, 10 commits). MIT-licensed and small enough to vendor, though it builds against a CUTLASS submodule and needs CUDA 12.9+ on Hopper or Blackwell.
